::: lead
I've been teaching since 2020, first mathematics and now data science. My goal is simple: help students become effective, hard-working, and ethical data workers.
:::

I try to teach the reasoning before the tools. Students should know what a model assumes and how it can fail before they reach for a library. I also want them to practice the whole job, not just the modeling step: version control, cleaning messy data, testing, deployment, and explaining results to someone who isn't a data scientist. And I want them to treat privacy, bias, and leakage as part of the engineering, not an afterthought.

## AI Teaching Fellow

In 2026 I was selected as an AI Teaching Fellow for the College of Engineering at the University of Arkansas. The fellowship supports faculty exploring new ways to bring AI into teaching, and I'll share what I learn here as the ideas take shape.

## Courses

### Generative and Agentic AI

Students build RAG systems, orchestration pipelines, and agentic workflows. We run local LLMs with Ollama, build pipelines with LangChain, and monitor them with LangSmith. I also developed versions of this course and an applied Python course for Arkansas's statewide data science program, for people looking to upskill or reskill. About 150 students have taken them so far, including about 80 members of the National Guard Reserve. These courses received the inaugural University of Arkansas Global Campus Award for Excellence in Course Design in 2025.

### Statistical Learning

I rebuilt this course around how modeling is done today: tidymodels, real data cleaning, and deployment with Docker and MLflow.

### Principles of Data Science

An introduction for about 80 incoming freshmen covering the data science process, the tools of the profession, and its ethics.

### Earlier teaching

- **Walton College of Business (2023 – 2024):** Python, R, Git, and Bash for 100+ students, plus advanced optimization projects in routing, network flow, and facility location with CVXPY, Pyomo, PySAL, and Gurobi.
- **Department of Mathematical Sciences (2020 – 2022):** precalculus, calculus, linear algebra, differential equations, and introductory statistics.
- **K–12:** data science, Python, and AI through the University of Arkansas [STEM Prep](https://stemprep.uark.edu/courses.php) program.

## Working with industry

I work with Mastercard, Walmart, Tyson, J.B. Hunt, Arvest Bank, and Dillard's to bring real data and real problems into my classes. Those partnerships turn into guest lectures, practicum projects, and, ideally, internships and jobs for students. If your organization is interested in working with our students, please [email me](mailto:sarafi@uark.edu).
